tasks.short: Check what is missing on the cart, restock it from the storage room, clean and tidy the storage area and cart, and report storeroom items running low.

steps.what: Housekeeper checks what is missing on the cart
Housekeeper keeps carts well-stocked from the storage room
Housekeeper keeps storage areas and carts clean and tidy
Housekeeper reports storeroom items running low: writes them on the supervisor's paper list in the office today; taps them on the supervisor's order list in the app on the spot after the change

tasks.design: Items running low in the storeroom are reported by tapping them in the housekeeping app on the housekeeper's phone ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which adds them to the supervisor's order list, instead of writing them on a paper list and finding the supervisor. Checking, restocking and tidying stay with the housekeeper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Low stock was written on a paper list that was often lost.
tasks.enabler_now: Housekeeping apps on phones take simple reports.
tasks.still_hard: Some housekeepers do not read the app's language well.
tasks.human_edge: Setting up a cart so the shift runs without trips back.

reach.learn: Whether low stock is reported in time.

evidence.claim: Housekeeping apps on phones can take low-stock reports and add them to an order list.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to low stock reported; ordering is outside.
Input contract: housekeepers have the app on a work phone; fallback is the paper list.

Checking, restocking and tidying keep their full time. s4 keeps 60 because noting each item stays and only the walk to the paper list or the supervisor drops. The note on the order list is an ordinary save in the app; the supervisor checks the list before ordering.
The app has icons for common items.
research_questions: Do stock-outs in the storeroom fall?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep for the housekeeper: the item icons are set and kept by the supervisor.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the paper list stays next to the storeroom, so little walking is saved and s4 keeps 85 (1.5); high: the list was far from the storeroom (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check which room supplies are used, replace glasses, linens, writing supplies and bathroom items, and handle guests' requests for extra items.

steps.what: Housekeeper checks which supplies in the room are used or missing
Housekeeper replenishes drinking glasses, linens, writing supplies and bathroom items
Reception enters the guest's request in the housekeeping app with room number and item
Housekeeper takes guests' requests for extra items: by phone from reception today; as tasks in the housekeeping app after the change
Housekeeper marks the request done in the app, which tells reception

tasks.design: Guest requests for extra towels, pillows or toiletries arrive as tasks in the housekeeping app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with room number and item, entered by reception, so the housekeeper is not phoned or tracked down; marking the task done tells reception. Checking and replenishing rooms stay with the housekeeper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by phone or a colleague searching the floors.
tasks.enabler_now: Housekeeping apps route requests to the housekeeper on the floor.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent requests still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing what a long-stay guest always runs out of.

evidence.claim: Housekeeping apps can route guest requests to the housekeeper on the floor.

assumptions: Boundary: from the room to clean to the request taken; front desk handling is outside.
Input contract: reception enters requests in the app; fallback is phoning.

Reception enters requests (s3r) in about the time a call took. s3 keeps 40 because reading the task replaces being phoned or tracked down on the floor. The done mark (s3d) is an ordinary save in the app and needs no approval.

incremental.description: No new work beyond the steps: the done mark is shown in s3d.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: reception still phones for urgent requests, so s3 keeps 70 (3.9); high: most requests arrive as tasks (7.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch for damage and security risks while cleaning, decide what to report, report damage or theft, log found articles, and bring them to the office.

steps.what: Housekeeper observes precautions to protect hotel and guest property while cleaning
Housekeeper decides what needs reporting
Housekeeper reports damage and theft: to supervisors in person or by phone today; after the change writes a report in the app with room, type and a photo that shows only the item
Housekeeper checks the report: room, what is damaged or missing, and that the photo shows only the item
Housekeeper submits the checked report to the supervisor in the app
Housekeeper writes found articles: in the lost-and-found book today, in the app with a photo and room number after the change
Housekeeper brings found articles to the housekeeping office

tasks.design: The housekeeper writes damage and theft reports in the housekeeping app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with room, type and a photo, checks each and submits it, which notifies the supervisor at once, so the housekeeper does not have to find or phone the supervisor; suspected theft in progress is still phoned. Found articles are written in the same app with a photo and room number instead of a paper book, which takes as long. Watching, deciding and handing in articles stay with the housekeeper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports depended on finding the supervisor and found articles were written in a book.
tasks.enabler_now: Housekeeping apps take photo reports and lost-and-found entries.
tasks.still_hard: Photos must not show guests or their papers.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that something in a room is not right.

evidence.claim: Housekeeping apps can take photo reports of damage and lost-and-found entries.
Found property must be kept and handled under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the room to clean to the article handed in; police reports are outside.
Input contract: housekeepers have work phones with the app; fallback is the book and phone.

Watching, deciding, logging found articles, the check and submit and handing in keep their full time. s3 keeps 60 because writing the report with a photo stays and only finding or phoning the supervisor drops.
Supervisors read app reports as they took calls.
research_questions: Are found articles returned to guests more often?

incremental.description: No new work beyond the steps: the photo is part of writing the report in s3.

approvals.approved_version: The damage or theft report with room, type and photo exactly as checked by the housekeeper in s3c, submitted once to the housekeeping supervisor in the app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: supervisors still want a call for most damage, so s3 keeps 80 (3.6); high: reports go through the app (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sort clean linens, count them, mark them, store them in linen closets, and write the counts on the linen sheet.

steps.what: Housekeeper sorts clean linens by type and size
Housekeeper counts clean linens
Housekeeper marks linens
Housekeeper stores linens in linen closets
Housekeeper writes linen counts on the linen sheet

tasks.design: Linens carry RFID tags, and the laundry's reader counts each delivery by type and records it in the linen system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the housekeeper does not count every piece or write counts on a sheet; counting becomes spot checks of the delivery. Sorting, marking and storing stay with the housekeeper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Linens were counted piece by piece and counts written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: RFID-tagged linen is counted by readers at delivery.
tasks.still_hard: Linen without tags still needs counting.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a stained sheet before it reaches a bed.

evidence.claim: RFID-tagged linen can be counted by readers at delivery and recorded by type.

assumptions: Boundary: from the linen delivered to counts recorded; laundry processing is outside.
Input contract: the laundry tags linen and runs the reader; fallback is counting by hand.
Sorting and storing do not change.
Laundry staff's time does not change.

incremental.description: Housekeeper reports count differences to the laundry.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: some suppliers' linen is not tagged, so about half is still counted and written by hand; s2 keeps 70 and s5 keeps 60 (9.5); high: all linen is tagged (19.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The housekeeper keeps cleaning, restocking, watching for risks and handling linen; paper lists, phoned requests, lost-and-found books and counting by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A housekeeper with fewer trips to find the supervisor.
